RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastMiddle EastPalestine president Mahmoud Abbas postpones legislative electionsNew date in September 2027 set for elections, as well as a vote on the presidencyMahmoud Abbas, Palestinian Authority president, postponed legislative elections scheduled for November. Photograph: Jeenah Moon/Bloomberg Sat Oct 10 2026 - 14:02 • 2 MIN READPalestine’s president Mahmoud ‌Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian ‌territories.

Abbas set a date of September 11th, 2027, for both presidential and legislative elections, ​the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.

Abbas’s decree cited “obstacles posed by Israeli measures” to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions ​for “free, fair and inclusive elections”.

It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and ⁠Gaza to participate in the polls.

There had been serious doubts that ‌the ‌Palestinian ​Authority vote would go ahead in late November.

[ Game over: Inside the ruins of Gaza’s football stadiumsOpens in new window ]

The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since ⁠2005-2006, after which Abbas’s rival, the Islamist group Hamas, ​seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.

The decree said Israeli military ‌attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and ​movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel’s continued ⁠withholding of Palestinian tax ⁠revenues, created challenges ​to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.

In Gaza, the decree pointed to “exceptional security and humanitarian conditions”, the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.

[ In pictures: Three years of war in GazaOpens in new window ]

Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to ‌Gaza and East ⁠Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.

The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation’s executive committee and consultations ‌with Palestinian factions and political forces.

It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive ​Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address ​challenges facing the electoral process. – Reuters
